statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump

statements.venue: Press release announcing the AI Regulator Act proposal with Sen. Bennet
statements.quote: Americans in Vermont and across the country are freaked out by the warnings of AI researchers, and I’m right there with them.

slowdown.note: Signed the 23 September 2026 letter asking for a formal agreement with China 'that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development'. This is a co-signed letter, not a statement in his own words.

pause.note: The co-signed letter asks for an agreement with China that would 'potentially' enact a mutual pause in frontier AI development, so the pause is conditional on China joining. Separately, his AI Regulator Act proposal with Sen. Bennet would let a regulator pause the public release of a risky model for up to six months, which is a pause on release rather than on development.

intl.note: Signed the 23 September 2026 letter urging President Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with China to slow down, and potentially mutually pause, frontier AI development.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI. The co-signed letter mentions that 'increased automation of AI research may lead to even faster advancement' as a concern raised by AI company employees, but does not call for a ban.

record: Signed the letter from 17 Democratic senators urging President Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with China on frontier AI guardrails, including slowing down and potentially mutually pausing frontier AI development.

Announced, with Sen. Bennet, the AI Regulator Act proposal: a new federal agency with pre-certification of frontier AI models, power to pause public release of models with potential for catastrophic risk for up to six months, and penalties of up to 15% of a firm's prior-year global revenue.
grade_reason: Welch signed the 23 September 2026 letter, which says frontier AI development could enable activities that threaten 'humanity writ large' and that 'the stakes are existential'. The grade rests on that co-signed letter; his strongest statement in his own words (being 'right there with' Americans alarmed by AI researchers' warnings) is level C.
notes: Six web searches ran, all successfully; no search was refused. Both statement pages were downloaded and each quote was checked by script to be an exact continuous passage of the page text (the Welch quote contains a curly apostrophe as on the page). All A and B evidence is from one co-signed letter; a reviewer may prefer to weigh his own-words statement (C) more heavily. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sanders and Casar, September 2026): no source found showing Welch as a co-sponsor; I did not check the congress.gov co-sponsor list directly. Not included as statements, because they are about topics outside the rubric's scope (level D) or predate 2025: joining a bill to block President Trump's executive order on state AI rules (press release 2026-01-07, seen in search results only, not opened), the TRAIN Act and NO FAKES Act on artists and copyright, AI chatbot letters on children's safety (2025-04-03), data center cost bills, the AWARE Act on AI in defense systems (2024), and the Trustworthy by Design AI Act (2024-12-23). A search summary mentioned an April 2025 letter with Sen. Rounds asking AI companies about safety practices; I could not find or open that page, so it is unverified and left out. A Vermont Public interview of 2025-01-06 ('Sen. Peter Welch wants to better regulate generative AI') appeared in results but was not opened. The Welch office tag page for artificial intelligence (pages 1 to 3 opened) showed no other releases on catastrophic risk.
